summary: GitHub lets developers register OAuth apps through a self‑serve web form at https://github.com/settings/applications/new, issuing a client ID and secret instantly with no review required for private apps. The process is free, takes only a few minutes of keyboard time, and the only prerequisite is that the developer's GitHub account has a verified email address (required for any OAuth authorization). If an account is flagged by GitHub, it cannot authorize third‑party apps until the restriction is lifted.

steps.title: Verify your email address
steps.detail: Ensure the GitHub account you will use to create the OAuth app has a verified email address, otherwise you cannot authorize the app later.

citations.quote: You must verify your email address before you can authorize an OAuth app.

steps.title: Open the OAuth app creation page
steps.detail: Navigate to the GitHub OAuth app creation form at https://github.com/settings/applications/new.

steps.title: Enter application details
steps.detail: Fill in the required fields: Application name, Homepage URL, Description (optional), and Authorization callback URL (the redirect URI your app will receive the code at).

steps.title: Create the app and retrieve credentials
steps.detail: Click "Register application". GitHub will generate a Client ID and a Client Secret. Copy both values and store them securely (e.g., in a password manager or secret vault).

steps.title: Configure scopes for your app (optional)
steps.detail: When you later request authorization, specify the scopes your app needs (e.g., repo, read:user). Note that source code access cannot be limited to read‑only.

citations.quote: Currently, you can't scope source code access to read-only.

nuances.title: Source code access cannot be read‑only
nuances.detail: GitHub does not provide a read‑only scope for repository content; any repo scope grants full read/write access.

citations.quote: Currently, you can't scope source code access to read-only.

nuances.title: Token issuance limits
nuances.detail: A maximum of ten tokens can exist per user/application/scope combination, and GitHub enforces a rate limit of ten new tokens per hour.

citations.quote: There is a limit of ten tokens that are issued per user/application/scope combination, and a rate limit of ten tokens created per hour.

nuances.title: Hourly token limit triggers re‑authorization prompt
nuances.detail: If you hit the hourly token creation limit, GitHub does not revoke existing tokens; instead, the next authorization attempt shows a re‑authorization prompt in the browser.

citations.quote: Hitting the hourly rate limit will not revoke your oldest token. Instead, it will trigger a re-authorization prompt within the browser

whenBlocked.situation: Account is flagged and cannot authorize third‑party OAuth apps
whenBlocked.action: Contact GitHub Support to resolve the restriction on the account.
